hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: fulfillment_partner=NorthPost is a suspected contributing factor

hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: channel=mobile is the driver (a big segment that co-occurs with NorthPost)

hypotheses_considered.why: Q9 failed on the whole window because NorthPost's refunds were raising the comparison rate. Retested outside NorthPost (Q10), it was ASSOCIATION_SUPPORTED: 0.2931 vs 0.0411 (z=3.98), and the lift held within partner, region and channel.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: product_sku=HDPH-200 is a second, independent suspected contributing factor

hypotheses_considered.why: Retested outside NorthPost (Q11), it was CONTRADICTED. Its lift vs the rest was -0.001, so it rose along with the overall spike.
Not tested directly because the tool budget ran out. Regions all have similar excess shares (about 22-28%). Electronics contains HDPH-200, so any electronics signal is probably that SKU.
hypotheses_considered.hypothesis: product_category=electronics or a particular region is the driver

final.hypothesis: Two independent suspected contributing factors: fulfillment partner NorthPost (primary) and SKU HDPH-200 (secondary, visible only outside NorthPost).
final.observed_anomaly: The refund rate in the current window was 26.75% (65 refunds out of 243 captures), against a baseline of 3.57%.
final.explanation: NorthPost accounts for most of the excess refunds (share 0.7194). Its refund rate was 40.18%, against 15.27% for the rest of the window and 4.4% for its own baseline. That lift held up after stratifying by every other dimension. Once NorthPost captures are excluded, HDPH-200 still stands out: 29.31%, against 4.11% for other captures outside NorthPost. This also held after stratifying, so it is a second, independent association. Mobile and SwiftShip-EU looked elevated only because they share volume with these drivers and rose with the overall spike. Both are associations, not proven causes.
final.uncertainty: These are statistical associations, not proven causes. Refund reason codes and individual transactions were not checked, so the mechanism (for example delivery failures at NorthPost or a defect in HDPH-200) has not been confirmed. Electronics and region were not tested directly because the tool budget ran out. Sample sizes are modest (112 NorthPost captures; 58 HDPH-200 captures outside NorthPost).
